frontmatter.title: Presentation: Structure & Evolution of the Australian Plate

children.value: The goal of this presentation is to give you the opportunity to apply some concepts from the course to understand the structure and evolution of the Australian Plate.

Select a topic related to the structure and evolution of the Australian Plate, building on the course lectures and the research-level talks given during the semester. You then deliver a short presentation (8 minutes including questions) and provide a short written summary that applies course concepts while incorporating additional background research. The goal is to communicate something interesting to your peers that demonstrates understanding of both the theoretical concepts and their application to the Australian geological context.
Aim for about 5 slides: the talk has to fit an 8-minute slot, including questions.

of about 500 words. This can be the script of your presentation with annotation, or presenter notes in the slides. It lets you add references and explanations that would otherwise spoil the flow of your talk. There are no penalties for going longer, but no advantages either.
Clearly identify the topic and how it relates to an aspect of the course.
Reference all figures and cite all data. On the slide a simple name / year citation is enough; give the full references after the final slide or in the presenter notes.
We assess your ability to present the topic and convey information. This is not about presentation style: it is about whether you can teach a complicated topic in a simple way.
You should be able to answer simple questions from your peers, to show that you have background knowledge of the topic.
These are outcomes 1, 2, 4 and 5 of the
Describe the broad geological history of the Australian plate and place its major structures in their tectonic context.
Explain the relationship between plate kinematics, plate tectonics forces and the deformation patterns in the continental crust.
Predict the geometry and location of structures at depth or in areas of poor outcrop through the use of geological and geophysical observations.
Interpret the relative timing of formation of structures, the kinematics of deformation, and progressive deformation histories in geological settings and laboratory / computer analogues.

Application of Course Concepts to Australian Plate Evolution (25 marks)

children.label: Application of Course Concepts to Australian Plate Evolution (25 marks)

children.value: Applies theoretical concepts from lectures to understand and explain specific aspects of Australian Plate structure and evolution

Applies course concepts effectively to the Australian Plate context. Uses appropriate examples (which may include modern tectonics, other plate settings, or direct Australian examples) to explain relevant concepts. Demonstrates clear understanding of how theoretical frameworks help interpret Australian Plate structure and evolution.

Applies course concepts well to the Australian context with reasonable examples. Shows good understanding of how theoretical frameworks relate to Australian Plate evolution. May rely more heavily on either modern or historical examples but makes solid connections.

Makes basic application of course concepts to the topic with some relevant examples. Shows adequate understanding of connections between theory and Australian Plate context, though may lack depth or clarity in some areas.

Makes weak or superficial connections between course concepts and geological settings. Struggles to demonstrate how theoretical frameworks apply to or illuminate the topic. Limited ability to show relevance to Australian Plate evolution or context. Connections between theory and examples are unclear or poorly developed.
Not addressed or contains significant misunderstandings of course concepts and their application to geological contexts.
Background research beyond lectures, synthesis with course content

Conducts thorough background research from appropriate sources. Successfully integrates research findings with lecture material to provide enriched understanding. Demonstrates ability to connect additional sources with course content into coherent narrative.

Conducts good background research from suitable sources. Integrates research findings reasonably well with lecture material. Shows ability to synthesize additional material with course content, though may lack some depth.
Conducts adequate background research. Makes basic integration of research with lecture material, though synthesis may be uneven. Shows some ability to connect additional sources with course content.

Weak integration of research with lecture material - tends to list facts or information rather than synthesizing into coherent understanding. Limited background research beyond lectures or relies on poor quality sources. Struggles to connect additional material meaningfully with course content.
Not addressed or contains significant misunderstandings of research integration and synthesis.
Ability to explain complex topics simply, clear teaching to peers

Communicates complex topics with clarity and effectiveness. Structures presentation logically to build understanding progressively. Successfully simplifies difficult concepts while maintaining scientific accuracy and engaging peer interest.
Communicates complex topics clearly with good structure. Simplifies difficult concepts reasonably well while maintaining accuracy. Engages peers with logical progression of ideas.
Communicates the topic adequately with basic structure. Makes some effort to simplify complex material, though clarity may be uneven. Generally understandable to peer audience.

Unclear explanations that are difficult to follow. Poor structure makes it challenging to understand the progression of ideas. Struggles to simplify complex material for peer audience - may use excessive jargon or fail to break down difficult concepts into accessible components.
Not addressed or demonstrates significant inability to communicate effectively.
Through written summary, presenter notes, and Q&A responses

Written materials demonstrate comprehensive understanding with clear explanations. Handles questions well, showing strong background knowledge and ability to discuss related concepts. Evidence of genuine comprehension rather than memorization.

Written materials show good understanding with clear explanations. Responds to questions reasonably well, demonstrating adequate background knowledge. Shows understanding beyond surface level in most areas.
Written materials show basic understanding. Answers straightforward questions adequately, though may struggle with more complex queries. Demonstrates acceptable grasp of core concepts.

Difficulty answering basic questions about the topic, showing limited background knowledge. Tends to repeat information from slides rather than demonstrating deeper understanding. Written summary and presenter notes lack depth or clarity. Struggles to discuss concepts beyond what is explicitly presented.
Not addressed or demonstrates significant lack of understanding of the topic.
Integration of Personal Lab/Field Experience (10 marks)

children.label: Integration of Personal Lab/Field Experience (10 marks)

children.value: Integrates their own laboratory, mapping, or field work experience to provide unique insights and authentic connections to the topic

Effectively integrates personal laboratory, mapping, or field work experience to provide unique insights. Makes authentic connections between their own hands-on work and the presentation topic. Uses personal experience to enhance understanding rather than just reference it.

Integrates personal lab/field experience well with good connections to the topic. Provides some unique insights based on own work. Shows reasonable ability to use personal experience to enhance understanding.

Makes basic connections between personal lab/field experience and the topic. Provides some personal perspective, though integration may be limited. Shows adequate effort to relate own work to the presentation.

Makes weak or superficial connections between personal lab/field experience and the topic. Tends to list activities or observations without providing insights or meaningful integration. Fails to demonstrate how personal experience enhances understanding of the topic.
Not addressed or fails to incorporate personal lab/field experience.
Proper referencing, figure citations, slide structure, presenter notes
All figures and data properly cited with complete references. Slide structure is clear and professional. Presenter notes are detailed and informative. References formatted correctly and complete.
Most figures and data properly cited with good references. Slide structure is clear and logical. Presenter notes are adequate and helpful. Minor issues with citation format or completeness.

Basic citation of figures and data with acceptable references. Slide structure is functional though may lack polish. Presenter notes provide basic information. Some inconsistencies in technical execution.

Missing or incomplete references for sources and figures. Poor slide structure makes presentation difficult to follow. Presenter notes are inadequate or missing, making slides hard to understand independently. Inconsistent or incorrect citation format.
Not addressed or demonstrates significant failure to meet technical standards.
